claims.claim: Posaconazole, a large lipophilic 1,2,4-triazole antifungal with a tetrahydropyran and high molecular weight, showed absolute oral bioavailability of 42–56% in the fasted state and 85–87% in the fed state, all above the 20% threshold.
Atazanavir, another high-molecular-weight/high-TPSA oral drug, showed >90% oral bioavailability when taken with food.
UDCA, a triterpenoid carboxylic acid, showed 78–87% systemic availability in cirrhotic patients, supporting that a triterpenoid acid scaffold can achieve high oral bioavailability.
No L1 record in any transferable context reports oral bioavailability below 20%; the lowest reported value is 35.9% for phenoxymethylpenicillin in underweight children.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule in humans or animals.
No specified prandial state or formulation for the query; food effects may be substantial for a lipophilic triazole triterpenoid.
Transferability from posaconazole, atazanavir, and UDCA contexts is inferred from structural and physicochemical similarity, not confirmed by query-specific pharmacokinetic data.
The query's zwitterionic character and very high estimated logP may affect absorption, but no quantitative permeability or solubility data are provided.
content.decision_summary: All transferable L1 records report oral bioavailability values above the 20% threshold, with the most relevant contexts (posaconazole, atazanavir, UDCA) showing 42–96% F. The physicochemical prior is an uncertain descriptor-based signal and is not affirmative evidence for F < 20%. Therefore F >= 20% is better supported.
